about: Taking part of a Social Security payment for a debt.

rows.plain: Under section 207 of the Social Security Act, most creditors cannot take Social Security benefits. Child support, alimony, federal taxes and some federal debts are exceptions.

For federal debts such as defaulted federal student loans, the Treasury Offset Program can take up to 15% of a Social Security retirement, survivor or disability payment, but must leave at least $750 a month.
SSI cannot be taken to collect a federal student loan.

Collection of defaulted federal student loans from Social Security has been paused and restarted more than once since 2025. Check your notice, or call the Default Resolution Group at 1-800-621-3115, for the current status.
Before an offset starts, the agency owed the money must send a notice saying how to see the records, ask for a review, or set up repayment.
When federal benefits are deposited directly, the bank must protect two months of benefits in the account from most garnishment orders.
